name: Cooper Scanlon
current_role: Co-founder, Movement Labs (not in Movement Network's current listed leadership)
profile: Co-founded Movement Labs with Rushi Manche to build Movement, a blockchain network based on Meta's Move language, which reached a ~$3B valuation in the 2024-25 crypto cycle. Movement Network is now stewarded by a Cayman foundation; its published leadership (CEO Torab Torabi, CSO Ali Sheikh) does not list him, and I couldn't verify his current role.
interesting_fact: Movement is built on Move, the asset-safe language Meta developed for financial applications, and now positions itself as a sub-second settlement and yield layer for emerging-market payments.

public_contacts.value: https://www.movementnetwork.xyz/contact (Movement general enquiries; company, not personal)

notes: Movement Labs had a 2025 leadership shake-up after the MOVE token market-maker controversy (co-founder Manche was removed); I couldn't confirm Scanlon's status in this pass because the web-search budget ran out. Check before outreach.

name: Alexandra Zatarain
current_role: Co-founder & VP of Brand and Marketing, Eight Sleep
profile: Co-founded sleep-tech company Eight Sleep in 2014 (YC S15) with Matteo Franceschetti (her partner) and CTO Massimo Andreasi Bassi. She leads brand and marketing for the Pod temperature-regulating mattress cover, positioned as 'sleep fitness'; Eight Sleep is valued around $2B and is pushing into health and China.
interesting_fact: She has said candidly that Eight Sleep 'was not intentional about our positioning for the first five years of the company' before landing on 'sleep fitness' - 'Now we know what to say yes to and what to say no to.'
deep_cut_fact: She ran the presentation at Eight Sleep's first-ever demo, a 'pajama party' at co-founder Max Andreasi Bassi's house in San Francisco showing a passive sensor mattress cover.
notes: Most media-facing co-founder after CEO Franceschetti; spoke at SXSW Sydney with him (SmartCompany). The co-founders shared hardware lessons with YC (May 2024): https://www.ycombinator.com/blog/lessons-on-building-hardware-from-the-founders-of-eight-sleep

name: Ryan Gury
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Innovation Officer, Performance Drone Works (PDW), Huntsville AL (CEO until James Slider took over)
profile: Drone engineer who designed and built the Drone Racing League's racing drones as its director of product, then co-founded PDW with Matt Higgins, Nicholas Horbaczewski and Trevor Smith. As CEO he led PDW to Army and SOCOM contracts for the C100 backpack quadcopter and a Huntsville 'Drone Factory 01'; PDW has an up-to-$820M conditional loan commitment from the Pentagon's Office of Strategic Capital.
interesting_fact: He says 'the C100 was designed backwards from a rucksack' - it can do ISR, laser target designation and supply drops, or act as a 'flying aircraft carrier' that quadruples FPV drone range.
deep_cut_fact: In 2017 he and his DRL engineers hand-built the DRL RacerX, which set a Guinness World Record for fastest battery-powered RC quadcopter: 163.5 mph official, with a 179.6 mph peak, from a drone under two pounds.

public_contacts.value: Boyd Bailey, Reputable PR - boyd@reputablepr.com (listed PDW media contact)

notes: Quotable, technical defense-drone voice; he co-wrote a July 2025 piece with David Hambling (linked from PDW news). Dual-use drone manufacturing and supply chains fit the podcast's energy/industrial angle.
